_note: B37 computer school: computing nouns in natural scenes – a ground-floor lab, an upstairs lab and a break corner; English sound-alike hooks acted on each item.

fr_seance_noun.hook: The tutor raises one finger: 'SAY it ONCE!' – SAY-ONCE, a lesson session (say-AHNSS).

fr_souris_noun.hook: The boy throws up his hands – 'SORRY!' – as the mouse he knocked off dangles by its cord (soo-REE).

fr_ressource_noun.hook: The girl goes back to the bookshelf, her SOURCE, again and again – RE-SOURCE (ruh-SOORSS).

fr_programme_noun.hook: The boy holds up his whole PROGRAM, printed out so long it spills to the floor (pro-GRAM).

fr_ordinateur_noun.hook: The old computer puts everything in ORDER – the ORDER-NATOR (or-dee-na-TUR).

fr_internet_noun.hook: The glowing globe is wrapped in a NET of lines joining every country – the INTERNET (an-tair-NET).

fr_systeme_noun.hook: The tall cabinet of blinking lights runs the whole SYSTEM (sees-TEM).

fr_code_noun.hook: Tap the secret CODE into the keypad on the wall (kod).

fr_reseau_noun.hook: The technician kneels to RE-SEW the torn web of blue cables – RE-SEW, the network (ray-ZOH).

fr_chercheur_noun.hook: The researcher holds out her notebook: 'SHARE? SURE!' – SHARE-SURE, the researcher (shair-SHUR).

fr_telecommunication_noun.hook: The big white dish on the roof beams calls far away – TELECOMMUNICATION (tay-lay-ko-mu-nee-ka-SYON).

fr_simulation_noun.hook: The boy flies through the clouds without leaving his seat – a flight SIMULATION (see-mu-la-SYON).

fr_suppression_noun.hook: She SUPPRESSES the mess – crumpled paper straight into the bin: deleted (su-pray-SYON).

fr_connexion_noun.hook: The two girls push the two cable ends together – a CONNECTION (ko-nek-SYON).

fr_protocole_noun.hook: The man in the grey suit ticks every step on his clipboard – he follows PROTOCOL (pro-to-KOL).

fr_moniteur_noun.hook: A huge MONITOR screen glows on the desk (mo-nee-TUR).

fr_automate_noun.hook: The little brass robot walks all by itself – an AUTOMATON, an AUTO-MATE (o-to-MAT).

fr_clavier_noun.hook: He plays the computer keyboard with both hands like an old CLAVIER, a piano (kla-VYAY).

fr_informatique_noun.hook: She opens the computer to INFORM her friend how it works inside – INFORM-ATICS, computer science (an-for-ma-TEEK).

fr_halte_noun.hook: She raises her palm: 'HALT! Time for a break' – and picks up her sandwich (alt).

fr_console_noun.hook: She CONSOLES her sad friend who lost the game on his console (kon-SOL).

fr_mail_noun.hook: He sends a MAIL from his laptop – shown flying off as a paper airplane (mel).

fr_logiciel_noun.hook: He breaks the red wax SEAL on the new box of software – LOGIC-SEAL (lo-zhee-SYEL).

fr_informaticien_noun.hook: The IT specialist works like an INFORMATION MAGICIAN – top hat, wand and toolbag (an-for-ma-tee-SYAN).

fr_donnee_noun.hook: A young scientist named Donny ("do-NAY") stands on a stool and presses a single red dot, one DATUM, onto a giant empty graph on the wall.
fr_donnee_noun.why: Donny ~ donnee; moved to the computing floor

fr_recepteur_noun.hook: In the armchair upstairs, a man presses the telephone RECEIVER to his ear in surprise, the rotary phone on the side table beside him (ray-sehp-TUHR).
fr_recepteur_noun.why: receptor ~ recepteur; moved from the hotel terrace to the telecom floor
